title: Magnon-dislon hybridization in magnetic insulators
authors: Carlos Saji, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Roberto E. Troncoso
abstract: Spin dynamics in ordered magnets with topological lattice defects is investigated. Using fracton--elasticity duality, we develop an effective field theory of magnons coupled to quantized lattice dislocations (dislons) in magnetic insulators. Within this framework, an elastic gauge field mediates a nonlocal interaction between dislocations and magnetization gradients. The resulting magnetoelastic coupling gives rise to coherent magnon-dislon hybridization whose properties are dictated by dislocation topology. Screw dislocations exhibit helicity-selective hybridization and symmetry-protected dark dislon sectors, while edge dislocations generate anisotropic hybrid excitations with finite spin-precession ellipticity through the glide constraint. Our results establish dislocations as dynamical topological defects with directly observable polarization fingerprints in magnon spectra, and reveal magnon-dislon hybridization as a new route to control spin dynamics.
summary: This theoretical paper develops an effective field theory for the interaction between magnons and quantized lattice dislocations in magnetic insulators. By analyzing the coupling strength based on dislocation topology (screw vs. edge), the authors predict distinct, observable signatures like helicity-selective modes or finite spin ellipticity. This highlights topological defects as controllable sources of novel quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates spin dynamics in ordered magnetic insulators when coupled to topological lattice defects, specifically dislocations (dislons). The goal is to develop a unified theoretical framework describing this magnon-dislon hybridization.
main_result: The coupling mechanism is highly dependent on the dislocation type: screw dislocations exhibit helicity-selective coupling and dark modes, while edge dislocations generate finite spin-precession ellipticity due to the glide constraint. This establishes defects as sources of observable polarization fingerprints in magnon spectra.
method: The authors develop an effective field theory using fracton–elasticity duality, recasting the dynamics into a gauge field framework. They calculate the coupled excitations by integrating out the elastic gauge field to derive a mixed magnon-dislon vertex.
model_or_system: The system is a ferromagnetic crystal containing embedded dislocations. The model uses an effective action $S_{	ext{eff}}$ describing the coupling between spin fluctuations (magnons) and dislocation vibrations (dislons), treated as coupled bosonic excitations.
key_observables: Magnon–dislon hybridization gap ($\Delta h$), polarization fingerprints, and finite spin-precession ellipticity ($E_n$) for edge dislocations.
important_parameters: The coupling strength $g$, the momentum transfer $\kappa$, and the distinction between screw vs. edge dislocation geometries are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: Approximations include linear order in small transverse dislon fields, assuming a strict quasi-one-dimensional limit for calculations, and using weak-coupling expansions near resonance.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral weights showing avoided crossings for screw dislocations and demonstrate the anisotropic coupling leading to elliptical polarization for edge dislocations.
paper_structure: The paper builds from deriving the full magnetoelastic action via gauge fields, calculating the propagator components, deriving the mixed vertex by integrating out the elastic field, and finally analyzing the resulting coupled quadratic Hamiltonian for both screw and edge geometries.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete example of how topological defects can introduce novel, geometrically constrained coupling channels into collective excitations (magnons), offering new avenues to control spin dynamics beyond simple bulk interactions.
